answer: Coordination Deposit Ladder. Each new identity must deposit a fee that rises along the vine of prior referrals, and only accounts reachable from a seeded island of verified nodes can transact, so a sybil cluster on an isolated terrace must fund a full ladder before any member gains a single usable slot. Every added identity also raises the marginal deposit for the whole sibling group, making each fake agent cost the attacker the cumulative ladder price rather than one flat fee. Attackers therefore pay superlinear capital that stays locked and forfeits on collusion detection.
